findings.title: Target members are deep-cloned even when the patch replaces or rebuilds them
findings.why: Each target member is cloned up front. If the patch then deletes it, replaces it, or recurses into it, that clone is discarded, and the recursion builds fresh objects at every level anyway. For deeply nested targets this repeats the deep copy at each level, which is quadratic work. Cloning only the keys the patch does not touch would give the same result with less copying.
